title: Setting the Next Goal Right Away
description:
The day {name} first hit 50 million won, before even celebrating, they set the next goal. '500 million won.'

That immediacy carried all the way here.

Today, before another milestone, that day came to mind.

choices.text: Like then — don't stop, look at the next number
choices.result_text:
A habit of not lingering on achievement.

That pushed {name} quickly to the next stage.
From 50 million won to 500 million won, that gaze eventually aimed at 3 billion won.

choices.text: This time, pause — acknowledge coming this far
choices.result_text:
Look only at next and you miss now.

{name} paused to acknowledge how far they'd come.
Arriving acknowledged versus arriving chased — the faces differ at the finish.

title: Asking What's Next
description:
When Hyun-su failed the exam, instead of comfort {name} asked practically, 'What will you do next?'

Today Hyun-su reached out.

'Hyung, you didn't comfort me — you asked about my next plan. That actually snapped me out of it.'

choices.text: "Because I believed you'd get back up."
choices.result_text:
'...That helped more than comfort would have.'

What a fallen person needs is sometimes not pity but the premise that they'll rise again.
{name} knew that instinctively.

choices.text: "I wished someone had asked me that too."
choices.result_text:
When you fall, 'what now' lifts you more than 'it's okay.'

{name} had offered Hyun-su the words they'd wanted to hear.
Giving what you never received — that's one way of growing up.

title: Asking About the Plan
description:
The day Hyun-su left the goshiwon, {name} asked, 'Do you have any idea what you'll do?'

Today word came from Hyun-su.

'Hyung, thinking about you asking me that, I actually made a real plan. I'm doing it now.'

choices.text: "Good. Seeing you plan, I know it'll work out."
choices.result_text:
'Thanks to you I turned something vague into something concrete.'

A single question changes someone's direction.
{name} was glad they'd asked instead of just sending him off.

choices.text: "Hearing your news fires me up too."
choices.result_text:
On separate paths, each other's progress became fuel.

News that Hyun-su had found his way spurred {name} too.
Two people who started in the same goshiwon, moving at their own speeds.

title: Just Walking Past
description:
While Hyun-su was drifting, {name} was too busy with their own affairs and just walked past.

Today they heard about Hyun-su by chance. He'd more or less landed on his feet.

Walking past that time nags sometimes.

choices.text: Reach out now, even late
choices.result_text:
Late, but reached out.

Hyun-su was unexpectedly glad. 'Hyung, long time.'
Doing now what couldn't be done then beat not doing it at all.

choices.text: I had no room then either — accept it
choices.result_text:
A drowning person can hardly save another.

{name} could barely keep themselves afloat then too.
You can't be good to everyone — they decided to accept that without guilt.

title: A Bowl of Ramyeon at the Door
description:
While Hyun-su was drifting, instead of words {name} cooked a bowl of ramyeon and left it at his door.

Today Hyun-su reached out.

'Hyung, that ramyeon at your door — that was you, right? You didn't say anything, but you cried a little eating it.'

choices.text: "It was nothing. You held on well."
choices.result_text:
'you'll never forget that ramyeon.'

A wordless bowl of ramyeon landed deeper than any words of comfort.
{name} knew it was repaying a debt for the dawn ramyeon they'd once received.

choices.text: "I once got ramyeon like that too."
choices.result_text:
'...So that's why you did it.'

Letting received warmth flow on to someone else.
That was the invisible connection making this tiny goshiwon bearable.

title: Calling Hyun-su After the Scam
description:
The day after being scammed by Jaehyuk, trying not to collapse, {name} called Hyun-su.

Today Hyun-su brought up that day.

'Hyung, you called me then. I remember your voice shaking. But you got back up the next day.'

choices.text: "I held on because you picked up."
choices.result_text:
'You did the same for me. That's what we are.'

Having someone to call when you're collapsing.
That was the rope that held {name} through that night.

choices.text: "Alone, I couldn't have gotten up."
choices.result_text:
Having even one person you can show weakness to.

{name} learned that's not the opposite of strength — it's part of the strength to rise again.

title: The Day I Did Nothing
description:
The day after being scammed by Jaehyuk, {name} lay around doing nothing all day.

That collapsed day comes back sometimes.

Today, after another hard thing, they're stalled like that day.

choices.text: That day was needed too — I rose after collapsing
choices.result_text:
It's okay not to rise right away the day after collapsing.

Because of that day's pause, starting again the next day was possible.
{name} decided to allow themselves time to fall apart too.

choices.text: This time, recover faster than that day
choices.result_text:
Back then, a whole day was lost. Now recovery came a little faster.

The collapsing is the same, but the speed of rising changed.
{name} felt how much sturdier they'd become.

title: Calling Dad Directly
description:
When {name} heard about Dad's medication, they called Dad directly instead of going through Mom.

Today Dad brought up that call.

'Minjun-ah. You called me directly that time, not your mother. That was — reassuring.'

choices.text: "It's about you, Dad. Of course I'd ask you directly."
choices.result_text:
'...Yeah. Thank you.'

Treating him as the person concerned, not as a patient.
Maybe that was what Dad needed more than the medication.

choices.text: "I'll always ask you directly from now on."
choices.result_text:
'You do that. I'm still fine.'

A faint pride colored Dad's voice.
One direct call closed a little of the distance between them.

title: Leaving Gracefully
description:
When leaving the job, {name} wrapped up politely with 'I'm sorry.'

Today a former coworker reached out.

'How are you? You handed everything over cleanly when you left — everyone remembers you well.'

choices.text: "How you end a relationship matters."
choices.result_text:
Someone who closes the door well when leaving.

That reputation may help again, who knows when or where.
{name} knew endings matter as much as beginnings.

choices.text: "It was a good experience, thanks to all of you."
choices.result_text:
A relationship ended well becomes an asset.

No telling what opportunity a former coworker might bring later.
{name} felt the choice not to burn bridges had been right.

title: Handing In the Notice Calmly
description:
When leaving the job, {name} resigned calmly: 'you've found something you need to do now.'

Is that conviction still valid?

That moment came to mind today.

choices.text: That conviction was right — no regrets
choices.result_text:
Stepping out of stability took courage.

That moment of decision brought {name} to the next stage.
An unwavering resignation letter turned the direction of a life.

choices.text: I was sure — but the road wasn't easy
choices.result_text:
Left calmly, but what followed wasn't calm.

{name} filled the gap between conviction and reality with their whole body.
Still, had they not left then, the present self wouldn't exist.

title: Just Stamping the Form
description:
When leaving the job, {name} just stamped the form and walked out without a word.

That cold ending comes back sometimes.

Passing near the old workplace today, that day came to mind.

choices.text: It was the best then — no reason to drag it out
choices.result_text:
Not every parting needs to be warm.

Sometimes a clean cut beats dragging things out.
{name} acknowledged that decisiveness was needed in that moment.

choices.text: Maybe I should've said goodbye — a little regret
choices.result_text:
A rough ending lingers in a corner of the mind.

{name} thought to wrap things up more smoothly next time.
Burning bridges should be done only when truly necessary.

title: Pretending Not to See
description:
When {name} ran into a successful classmate at a restaurant, they pretended not to see and found a corner seat.

That avoidance comes back sometimes.

Today, a similar situation — heard someone's doing well.

choices.text: I don't avoid anymore — I stand tall in my place
choices.result_text:
Back then, hid for fear of comparison. Now, having a path, they stand tall.

{name} knows another's success isn't their failure.
The self who sought corners can now sit in the middle.

choices.text: Avoiding then — was also a way of protecting myself
choices.result_text:
When you're sure to be shaken, avoiding is one method.

No need to throw yourself into an unprepared comparison.
{name} reframed that avoidance not as weakness but self-protection.

title: Speaking Honestly
description:
When {name} ran into a successful classmate, they didn't avoid it — they walked over and spoke honestly.

That candor comes back sometimes.

Today that classmate reached out. 'What you said back then stuck with me.'

choices.text: "Honesty's easier. You doing well too?"
choices.result_text:
Stating your situation without dressing it up.

That actually drew out the other's respect.
{name} wasn't ashamed of having been honest in the face of comparison.

choices.text: "Talking with you back then fired me up too."
choices.result_text:
Turning comparison into fuel was possible only by facing it head-on.

{name} carried that conversation as a spur, not envy.
The same encounter becomes poison or medicine depending on how you meet it.
